title: Native activation and authorization-code handoff
prerequisites: Required: run sdk_native_preflight against the selected environment before building or activation. Native KSSIDP uses BDDKEnrollment/BDDKLogin, useTokenBasedLogin=true, astServerBackend=maverick and login header X-KOBIL-ASTUSERID. The WebView alternative is KSTrustedWebView with explicit deployment clients. Missing clients or incompatible bindings block progress; never create substitute flows.
These bindings target classic MCSDK with KSSIDP; standalone IDPSDK needs its own adapter and is not interchangeable.
SDK initialization completed and activation is allowed by current state.
Existing server application/version has a selected registration user.
An explicitly selected native-compatible IDP client/flow and a valid activation user/code are available.

Decide the local authentication mode BEFORE the key-creating activation step. On Android the user-authentication policy is bound at Keystore key creation and cannot be changed on existing keys; changing it later requires discarding keys and a fresh activation with a new activation code (runtime-verified, 2026-09-29 validation round).

Mandatory agent gate: before activation call sdk_deployment_preflight(mc_config_path, expected_mtls) using actual configuration and explicit customer deployment choice, never a sample default. Explicit-auth TMS always requires require_explicit_authentication=true and expected_token_client from observed token ownership. Set granted_scope_stage=current (default) for the existing token: missing tms warns/pends verification, NOT blocks, because SDK StartTransaction may acquire it through exchange/step-up. Set granted_scope_stage=explicit_auth for the actual resulting token: granted_scopes must contain tms, otherwise missing scope/evidence blocks. Requested/assigned scopes are not actual granted-token evidence. The tool verifies supplied metadata only (configuration_checked, runtime acceptance false), not issuer capability, live token validity or backend acceptance; no policy enforcement on independent raw service API calls.

Mandatory before a physical iOS install: sdk_ios_signing_preflight(app_path, expected_team_id, device_udid) must inspect the actual built .app signature, signer DER certificate membership in the profile, profile-authorized entitlements and target eligibility. Wildcard authorization is limited to verified Apple application/keychain identifier patterns; do not generalize wildcard matching to other entitlements. Keep customer signing-team preferences in local project configuration, never public defaults. No fallback team or install based only on project settings/build success; resolve mismatch/missing prerequisites first. Artifact-only checks without device_udid do not establish device eligibility. Do not uninstall an activated app to repair a cross-team update without the required data-preservation/removal authorization.
sequence:
## Mobile identity and AST registration

Android applicationId and iOS bundle identifier are mobile application identities.
AST app_name and its registered version identify backend registration records;
they are not automatically the same identifier. A new mobile bundle ID alone
neither proves an existing AST registration is incompatible nor proves it reusable.
Never recommend adopting the SuperApp mobile bundle ID just to reuse its assets.

For an authorized app integration, proceed with sdk_app_list, sdk_app_get and
sdk_app_versions without asking for another confirmation for these read-only
checks. Inspect the selected platform/version, registration user, lock state,
integrity policy, and any signing/package binding required by the supplied SDK
and deployment. If returned metadata cannot establish a required binding, identify
that exact gap; do not claim compatibility from the app name or integrity flag alone.
Reuse a suitable existing app/version and preserve its registration user and
security policy. Create new records only when none is suitable or the user requests
separate registration. Do not disable integrity to force reuse.

Do not assert that a delivered sdk_config.jwt is bound to a mobile package or AST
app/version without inspecting the documented configuration contract and applicable
claims privately. sdk_config_write in this MCP takes certificates and connection
service settings, not a mobile bundle ID or AST app_name. Obtain a fresh
backend-signed configuration when required; never edit signed JWT contents.

Preserve the user's previously selected test security policy and flow. Ask only
for an unresolved binding/policy choice or an actual blocker; do not request the
same decision repeatedly. A test selection is not a default for other customers.

## Signed configuration and retained choices
Within an authorized app build, request a fresh signed SDK configuration with
sdk_config_write using the selected environment service map and verified public
TLS certificates. Do not ask the user to supply a JWT or propose trying an
unverified sample JWT when the MCP can issue one. If certificates, permissions
or services are missing, report that concrete prerequisite; never disable TLS
verification or edit a signed configuration.
Read project instructions (including CLAUDE.md when present) for previously
selected test policy before asking again. Reuse an explicit current-project
ALLOW_VIRTUAL_SMART_CARD/device-PIN decision; do not extend that test choice to
other projects. This does not authorize changing shared backend security policy.

## Authentication-mode matrix and preferred method (verified 2026-09-29 validation round, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231)

iOS KSMAuthenticationMode offers only no/biometric/password modes; there is no
PIN mode. Android offers device-credential and biometric authentication classes.
On Android the user-authentication policy is bound at Keystore KEY CREATION and
cannot be changed on existing keys: switching mode afterwards requires discarding
the keys and a fresh activation with a new activation code. Make and record the
mode decision before the key-creating activation step.

Preferred method (user decision recorded 2026-09-29 validation round): trusted WebView enrollment and
interactive login combined with SignedJWT token-based returning login
(useTokenBasedLogin=true, SE-signed JWT OfflineLogin), protected by device
biometrics/face recognition — iOS biometric mode; Android BIOMETRIC_STRONG with no
device-credential fallback. PIN/password/no-authentication remain documented
alternatives, not defaults. Never silently fall back from the selected biometric
policy to make a test pass.


Decision gate (Android PIN-prompt surprise, 2026-09-29 round): an explicit
authentication-mode decision is REQUIRED before activation. Activation guidance
or automation without a declared mode must produce a BLOCKING prompt/warning to
the user - never proceed on a silent default, because the first activation binds
the policy (on Android at Keystore key creation) and an unwanted mode costs an
uninstall plus a fresh activation code to undo. Authentication-mode enum values:
no=0, biometric=1, password=2, pin=3 (iOS 15.16 exposes no PIN mode). The
preferred method is biometric (user decision); record the chosen mode with the
run evidence.
Choose the existing deployment client and authentication mode explicitly; do not create a replacement flow to fit a sample.
Collect only the fields required by the selected activation flow; keep credentials out of logs.
Drive the native IDP wrapper or version-matched authorization-code bridge. Continue intermediate challenges rather than assuming one request.
Handle the authorization-code result and SDK activation outcome separately.
Query local user/device state and perform a subsequent login as separate acceptance checks.

## Native trusted WebView callback contract (verified 2026-09-29, Android MCSDK 15.16.3088426 / iOS MCSDK 15.16.803.3089231)

Record the callback contract from the ACTUAL delivered interfaces (javap/bytecode
on Android, synthesized Swift interfaces on iOS); do not code against assumed or
older signatures.

- Android (TWV Proxy 20.1): the delivered TWVClient only calls
  sendOpenIdRedirectUriCode from shouldOverrideUrlLoading(WebView, String) and
  onReceivedSslError. Android WebView does NOT invoke shouldOverrideUrlLoading for
  POST-initiated navigations, so the redirect after the enrollment POST is never
  delivered: activation stalls while the activation code is consumed. Verified fix:
  a TWVClient subclass intercepts the registered redirect URI in
  shouldInterceptRequest/shouldOverrideUrlLoading before any network request,
  matching the delivered nullable parameter signatures exactly - a signature
  mismatch silently fails to override. Second attempt returned
  SetAuthorisationCodeResult OK/error 0.
- iOS (KSTrustedWebView 9.7.3000479): ALL KsTrustedWebViewDelegate methods are
  required - the 15.16 header declares no @optional methods. Implement every one.
- Redirect validation on both platforms: exact scheme, host, effective port and
  path plus the state parameter; deliver the authorization code exactly once, then
  hand it to SetAuthorisationCode with the same client/tenant and mode. Ignore
  duplicate callbacks after consumption.
- Before any retry, read back the backend fixture (sdk_idp_user_credentials_list,
  sdk_ast_find_client): a stalled or failed enrollment can consume the activation
  code and create a password credential or partial AST client.
expected_result: Activation completes and the expected SDK local user/device is present; subsequent login is checked separately.
checklist: Valid activation completes and the expected local user/device exists.
Invalid/expired code produces a visible failure without automatic code reissue.
Activation user is not confused with the application registration user.
Mobile bundle/package identity and AST app/version are distinguished; reuse decision is supported by registration, integrity and applicable binding evidence.

Explicit authentication-mode decision (enum no=0, biometric=1, password=2, pin=3; preferred: biometric) made, recorded and confirmed BEFORE the key-creating activation step; missing decision blocks activation with a prompt instead of a silent default. On Android a later mode change requires key discard plus fresh activation with a new activation code.
Redirect interception delivers the authorization code exactly once with validated scheme/host/effective port/path and state; callback signatures match the delivered interface.
Forced trust/load failure in the trusted WebView shows a visible sanitized diagnostic (numeric error code + hint, no URLs or secrets); a blank page is impossible in the reference integration.
failure_handling: A server-issued code is required; device UI status cannot generate one.
A timeout may follow a consumed code. Inspect state before trying a new code.
Never recommend SuperApp Login V2 for native Android/iOS.
Never disable useTokenBasedLogin to work around ast_login_with_unactivated_client; this skips IAM setup and can cause CannotAcquireTokenData(50). Investigate the selected native backend flow instead.

Swift: switch on KssIdpStatus.success/eventFailed/requestFailed; never infer success from text containing accept. Preserve detailed callback status, errorCode and underlying event without logging tokens or credentials.

A later authentication-mode change on Android is not a configuration edit: the policy is bound at Keystore key creation. Discard keys and perform a fresh activation with a new activation code; never reuse a consumed code (runtime-verified, 2026-09-29 validation round).

Activation stalls after the enrollment POST with no redirect callback: verified Android cause is the delivered TWVClient not receiving shouldOverrideUrlLoading for POST navigations (TWV Proxy 20.1); intercept the registered redirect URI with exact delivered signatures. Read back fixture state before consuming another activation code.

Never blank-fail the WebView (VAL-36, 2026-09-29): the X1-only pinning failure on Flutter iOS rendered a SILENT white/blank page with no user-visible error, and the gap was only found by chain inspection. In the reference integration a blank page must be IMPOSSIBLE: wire onWebResourceError/onWebResourceHttpError (Flutter NavigationDelegate), the trusted-WebView failure callbacks (onURLBlocked/KS_CERTIFICATE_ERROR, load-failure delegate methods) and every TLS-failure path to a visible in-app diagnostic view that replaces the WebView content and shows the numeric error code, the phase and a sanitized hint (for example 'certificate validation failed - check the pinned trust anchors'), never URLs, hostnames, tokens or other secrets. Surfacing the error never means weakening or disabling validation. Tests must force a trust failure and assert the diagnostic view appears instead of a blank page.

When SDK reports FAILED/errorCode=0 and no Warning/RuntimeError/FatalError, inspect sanitized native SDK and HTTP diagnostics; listener silence is not absence of an error. Distinguish issuer TLS_CLIENT_WITH_KEY rejection 510000015 (mTLS deployment mismatch), HTTP403 Client is not the holder of the token wrapped as 700000022 (token holder versus IAM exchange client), missing explicit tms scope 516004034, and freshness failure 516004035. Numeric wrappers alone do not establish the cause; retain operation/status/explanation without tokens.

Swift trusted-WebView callbacks: inspect the delivered return/decision semantics and cancel only the verified authorization redirect. Do not cancel all nonredirect/external navigation; preserve the existing allowlist and certificate checks. Query versus fragment response parsing is scoped to the selected verified journey, never a reason to broaden endpoint/state validation or substitute another themed client/flow.

platform_notes.android: NativeActivationViewModel handles SetAuthorisationCodeResultEvent; IdpNativeInterfaces defines activation input mappings.
platform_notes.ios: KssIdpModel has separate activate calls for credential dictionaries and appDelegate-driven multi-step activation.
